Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become a vital tool for analyzing local atomic arrangements in materials. However, a significant challenge remains in defining the most effective GNN architecture to accurately quantify these configurations. This study introduces a systematic approach to assess the performance of various GNN models by establishing a rigorous mathematical framework for the "information content" of atomic environments. We define this information content as the mutual information between an environment and its corresponding representation, which we approximate using the Kullback-Leibler divergence. By applying this metric, we evaluate several state-of-the-art GNNs and determine that the SchNet model delivers the most information-rich representations of atomic environments.

This paper examines the application of weak convergence to estimate functions of parameters within statistical models. It establishes the general conditions required for the consistency and asymptotic normality of such estimators. The findings are illustrated through an analysis of the sample mean and the sample covariance matrix.

Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to model individual student learning trajectories by analyzing historical interaction data to forecast future performance. Despite the widespread adoption of deep learning in this domain, rigorous assessment of these methods remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-quality, real-world datasets. To address this, we introduce a novel, publicly available synthetic dataset called **Synthia**, which simulates the learning behaviors of thousands of students across diverse knowledge concepts. Built upon a knowledge graph that maps concept dependencies, Synthia generates realistic student interactions and associated quiz outcomes. We evaluated Synthia's efficacy using multiple deep learning-based KT approaches, demonstrating its ability to support accurate predictions for both individual students and specific knowledge items. Furthermore, we developed a new deep learning model that leverages the structural information inherent in the underlying knowledge graph.

This text presents a proof demonstrating that the second-order elliptic differential operator $L$, defined on smooth functions with compact support within a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, is surjective when $n \geq 3$.

The veriT theorem prover, introduced in 2009, supports a variety of output formats for both human and machine verification. The initial version of the veriT proof format was presented during the PxTP workshop in 2010. Since then, it has undergone several updates to enhance its capabilities, including the addition of lemmas, support for non-linear arithmetic, and features for interactive proof generation. This document provides a summary of the format's history and details the most recent version, veriT 1.1, which incorporates support for SMTLIB 2.

Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients while preserving data privacy, yet it often suffers from reduced scalability due to the heavy communication overhead of exchanging full model updates. To address this, FedBuff introduces a novel FL framework that combines local model buffering with differential privacy (DP). In this setup, each client maintains a local buffer containing multiple copies of the global model, which are updated locally and aggregated to form a client model. This client model is then transmitted to the server with added DP noise, ensuring privacy. On the server side, these noisy client models are averaged to refresh the global model. FedBuff offers significant advantages: it drastically cuts communication costs by exchanging only compact model buffers rather than full updates, and it maintains a strong theoretical guarantee of DP. Furthermore, the algorithm is highly flexible, supporting various local aggregation strategies and different DP noise injection points. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedBuff achieves superior performance compared to existing methods, delivering both enhanced training efficiency and robust privacy protection.

This study investigates cross-lingual speech recognition performance, specifically examining how pre-training on source languages influences models trained on target languages. We evaluate the impact of varying degrees of linguistic distance between these languages and compare results against monolingual pre-training baselines. Our analysis reveals that while pre-training on linguistically similar languages yields performance gains, the benefits diminish significantly when the source and target languages are dissimilar. Furthermore, we observe that the advantage of monolingual pre-training often surpasses that of cross-lingual pre-training when applied to target languages with substantial differences from the source.

This paper introduces SPGP-SARSA, a novel hybrid algorithm that integrates the strengths of both the Stochastic Path Integral Control (SPIC) and SARSA frameworks. Designed specifically for underwater navigation, the method leverages SPIC to perform high-precision policy evaluation while utilizing SARSA for efficient value function updates. By combining these techniques, the algorithm achieves a substantial reduction in computational cost compared to standard SPIC. Furthermore, the inclusion of SARSA's bootstrapping mechanism accelerates convergence, allowing the system to adapt more rapidly to dynamic environmental changes.

This study examines the relationship between relativistic stellar models involving two fluids and those with a single fluid. We demonstrate that solutions for the two-fluid system can be obtained from single-fluid solutions through a specific transformation. Conversely, we derive the corresponding single-fluid solutions from the two-fluid framework. We apply these transformations to analyze specific stellar models, including the Tolman IV and Tolman VII solutions, as well as the Ellis and Bronstein models.

This paper introduces a new method for English correction (GEC) adaptation that leverages pre-trained models on small, labeled datasets. The approach employs multi-task learning, where the primary task involves correcting the target language using minimal data, while auxiliary tasks utilize large-scale unlabeled datasets from other languages. To enhance the model's ability to extract features from these auxiliary tasks, we incorporate a dynamic gating mechanism that selectively integrates relevant information. Experiments demonstrate that this proposed adaptation strategy significantly outperforms standard multi-task transfer learning baselines, achieving results comparable to those obtained through multi-task learning with auxiliary labeled data.

We introduce a novel, deterministic, and efficient algorithm for dividing a divisible good among $n$ agents. This method generalizes the well-known "cut-and-choose" protocol to accommodate any number of participants. The algorithm guarantees that every agent receives a piece they value at least as highly as $1/(n-1)$ of the total good, according to their own valuation. Furthermore, the resulting allocation is envy-free with respect to these valuations. We demonstrate that this procedure is Pareto optimal and, when combined with the Round-Robin distribution strategy, yields an allocation that is both envy-free and proportionate. Additionally, we establish a lower bound of $n-1$ on the number of cuts required to achieve proportionality under the Round-Robin approach, proving that no algorithm can guarantee fewer cuts while maintaining these fairness properties.

We have conducted a comprehensive analysis of the HII region population in UGC 8839, a nearby, intermediate-mass spiral galaxy. Using the [OIII] 5007 Å emission line, we mapped the HII regions to create a 2D distribution map and a 1D histogram of their galactocentric radii. Our findings indicate that UGC 8839's HII regions are distributed across galactocentric radii ranging from 0.5 to 4.5 kpc. When compared to similar regions in other spiral galaxies, the radial distribution in UGC 8839 appears shifted toward larger galactocentric radii. Furthermore, the HII region population in this galaxy exhibits a bimodal distribution, with peaks located at approximately 1.5 kpc and 3.0 kpc. We attribute this bimodality to the presence of two distinct star-forming rings, which we identified through a 2D [OIII] 5007 Å image and a 1D surface brightness profile along the galaxy's major axis. Finally, we determined the star formation rate (SFR) to be 0.07 M☉/yr by applying the Kennicutt (1998) relation to the total [OIII] 5007 Å luminosity.

This study presents lattice QCD calculations of the pion's electromagnetic form factor, $G_E(Q^2)$ and $G_M(Q^2)$, across a range of quark masses, varying the pion mass from 350 MeV down to 270 MeV. The simulations employ $2+1$ flavor Wilson clover fermions on a $32^3 \times 64$ lattice with a lattice spacing of approximately 0.09 fm. The results indicate that as the pion mass decreases, the form factor exhibits a steeper decline at higher momentum transfers, a behavior consistent with expectations from chiral perturbation theory. Additionally, the study analyzes the sensitivity of the pion's charge radius to quark mass variations.

We present high-cadence, multi-band photometric observations of the classical T Tauri star AA Tau, collected over a 10-year period using the 1.5-meter Nordic Optical Telescope. These data reveal extreme variability in the accretion rate, characterized by a power spectrum with a slope of approximately 2.5 and a red noise component. This variability is notably more pronounced than what is observed in other classical T Tauri stars. We argue that this phenomenon is driven by changes in the inner disk structure, specifically the behavior of the inner gap and its associated dust ring. Consequently, these findings suggest that disk evolution in AA Tau occurs on timescales significantly shorter than those predicted by standard viscous evolution models.

Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) presents a significant hurdle because agents must learn from historical, potentially suboptimal data without the ability to interact with the environment. To address this, we introduce a new framework called Shared Individual Trajectories (SIT) that reorganizes offline data into multiple distinct trajectories, each anchored by a single shared agent. This transformation allows the problem to be tackled using standard single-agent reinforcement learning (SARL) techniques. Furthermore, we propose a specific offline multi-agent DQN algorithm built upon this framework. Our approach effectively leverages the inherent diversity within offline data to accelerate convergence and achieve higher performance than traditional offline MARL methods. We validate our framework's efficacy through experiments on the classic Taxi domain and a real-world scenario involving traffic light control.

This study introduces a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) framework designed to enhance image registration, specifically optimizing the initial alignment of images. The proposed method utilizes a CNN to generate an initial estimate of transformation parameters, which subsequently refines the result through an iterative optimization process. This strategy aims to overcome the limitations of conventional intensity-based registration techniques, which frequently suffer from poor convergence when starting from suboptimal initial conditions. The efficacy of the suggested approach is demonstrated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, with performance metrics compared against established registration algorithms.

We demonstrate that nonlocal effects and steering can emerge even when only one particle is entangled, provided the particles are spatially separated. We introduce a new form of nonlocal steering, grounded in the concept of particle indivisibility, which is induced by the entanglement of a single particle. This phenomenon is characterized by the ability to remotely steer the position of one part of a system using the position of another part, while simultaneously steering the momentum of one part using the momentum of another part. We further show that this type of nonlocal steering is distinct from and cannot be explained by standard Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering.

Blockchain technology offers a promising solution for enhancing data security and privacy within the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). This paper introduces a novel blockchain-based authentication protocol designed to address authentication and authorization challenges in IoV environments. The proposed protocol leverages blockchain to establish a secure, decentralized authentication framework, utilizing a hierarchical key management system to ensure efficient and robust access control. Furthermore, the study presents a comprehensive performance evaluation of the suggested protocol, demonstrating its superior efficiency and reliability compared to existing methods.

The V392 Persei system, a recurrent nova involving a white dwarf and a companion star, underwent a nova eruption in 2010. Post-eruption observations indicate that the system's accretion state shifted from the high/intermediate state to the low state, a transition that persisted for at least a year. We present new optical and near-infrared data collected approximately 1,000 days after the event, revealing that the system had returned to the high/intermediate state. Furthermore, our analysis of the post-eruption optical spectrum suggests the presence of a dense, expanding shell of material.

This paper introduces a feedback encoding scheme designed to enhance the efficiency of base station (BS) selection in cellular networks. The proposed method offers a significant advantage over conventional Lloyd clustering by eliminating the need for extensive pilot overhead during the clustering process. Instead, it utilizes a lightweight pilot structure where each BS transmits a single pilot, and user equipment (UE) identifies the BS with the strongest signal strength to report its index. This index is then quantized using a feedback codebook, which is optimized to minimize the total quantization error across all UEs. Simulation results demonstrate that the scheme achieves a low quantization error while requiring significantly less pilot overhead compared to traditional Lloyd-based approaches.

Surface currents, which are robust against disorder and characterized by a quantized value, have previously been identified in both bosonic and fermionic systems. This work demonstrates that surface currents also manifest in mixed statistics ensembles, specifically within a model of non-interacting fermions and bosons coexisting in a three-dimensional topological insulator. We derive the precise quantization condition for these currents, which depends on the statistical parameter $\eta$ (where $\eta=+1$ for bosons, $\eta=-1$ for fermions, and $\eta=0$ for mixed statistics). Furthermore, we analyze the spatial distribution of these currents, revealing that while surface currents in pure bosonic or fermionic systems are strictly confined to the boundary, in mixed statistics ensembles, they extend into the bulk. This bulk presence is governed by the statistical parameter $\eta$, with the currents decaying exponentially away from the surface over a characteristic length scale that varies with $\eta$.

This study examines the conditions for a photon to reach null infinity within the Brans-Dicke framework, specifically when a compact object emits scalar gravitational radiation. The analysis focuses on the interplay between the scalar charge and the mass of the radiating body. It is demonstrated that if the scalar charge is sufficiently small, the Brans-Dicke metric asymptotically approaches the Schwarzschild solution, thereby permitting photons to escape. Conversely, if the scalar charge is large, the metric exhibits a "no-hair" structure characterized by a naked singularity, which prevents photons from reaching infinity. The critical threshold separating these two regimes is determined as a function of the Brans-Dicke coupling parameter $\omega$.

We have conducted a study on Population III binary remnants, specifically focusing on the merger rate density of black hole-neutron star (BH-NS) and black hole-black hole (BH-BH) binaries. Our analysis indicates that the rate density for both BH-NS and BH-BH mergers reaches its maximum at a redshift of approximately $z \approx 1.5$. At this peak, the rate density is estimated at roughly $10^{-4} \text{ Gpc}^{-3} \text{ yr}^{-1}$ for BH-NS systems and approximately $10^{-5} \text{ Gpc}^{-3} \text{ yr}^{-1}$ for BH-BH systems. Consequently, the total integrated number of such events throughout cosmic history is projected to be around $10^4$ for BH-NS mergers and $10^3$ for BH-BH mergers. These findings suggest that Population III remnants could potentially be detectable by current gravitational wave observatories like LIGO/Virgo, as well as future facilities such as Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.

This study investigates the joint optimization of power allocation and secrecy rates within a multi-user, multi-antenna downlink system. In this setup, both legitimate users and eavesdroppers are equipped with multiple antennas, and the optimization framework incorporates non-convex constraints to model the secrecy rate requirements for each user. To address this challenge, we propose a novel alternating optimization algorithm. This approach iteratively refines power allocation and secrecy rates, utilizing a specific non-convex relaxation technique to handle the rate constraints. Furthermore, we employ a majorization-minimization strategy to optimize power distribution while maintaining fixed secrecy rates. The proposed method is validated through numerical simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing the overall security of the communication system.

Text games serve as an effective method for training and assessing language models, yet the textual nature of gameplay often slows down simulation. To address this, TextWorldExpress introduces a C-based text game engine that accelerates simulation by a factor of 100 compared to Python-based systems like TextWorld. This engine supports TextWorld's task, including its semantic interface, and has been used to reimplement TextWorld's dataset with a 100x faster simulation speed. Additionally, TextWorldExpress has been adapted to run the ReAct framework for autonomous agents, achieving a 99.5% success rate on its dataset while executing simulations 100 times faster than Python implementations.

Tensor decomposed model-oriented hardware has historically been the primary approach for deploying deep neural networks on embedded systems. However, this method suffers from significant latency and low throughput due to the extensive memory traffic required for loading decomposed tensors. To address these bottlenecks, we introduce a novel hardware architecture based on full-decomposed LSTM (FDHT-LSTM) that is optimized for high-throughput, low-latency operation. This architecture leverages a full-decomposed representation of LSTM weights and utilizes a specialized dataflow strategy to minimize memory access overhead. Our evaluation demonstrates that the proposed FDHT-LSTM architecture achieves a 2.3x increase in throughput and a 2.3x reduction in energy consumption compared to existing tensor decomposed model-oriented hardware.

We introduce a new version of the Weak Gravity Conjecture (WGC) applicable to anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, grounded in the concept of self-binding energy. This version posits that for any particle type with mass $m$ and charge $q$ existing in AdS, there must be an available multi-particle state composed of these particles that is both lighter than the single particle ($m_{\text{multi}} < m$) and carries a total charge exceeding that of the original particle ($q_{\text{multi}} > q$). We demonstrate that this condition is a natural extension of the standard, flat-space (Minkowski) WGC. Furthermore, we show that this AdS-specific conjecture imposes a strict upper limit on the AdS curvature radius when expressed in terms of the particle's mass and charge.

This paper investigates the submodule of zero elements within local cohomology modules, denoted as $(H^i_{\mathfrak{a}}(R))_0$. We examine the relationship between this submodule and the function characterizing the $\mathfrak{a}$-finiteness of a local ring $(R,\mathfrak{m})$. Furthermore, we establish that if the ring $R$ is F-rational, then the submodule $(H^i_{\mathfrak{a}}(R))_0$ must vanish for all $i < \text{ht}(\mathfrak{a})$.

This paper examines the all-or-none order design of the German redispatch market, analyzing its impact on procurement costs and the ability to clear the system. We introduce a new optimization model that integrates redispatch operations with generation scheduling to simulate market outcomes. Our analysis reveals that, under all-or-none rules, the grid operator must determine the total required redispatch volume upfront, compelling market participants to bid based on this aggregate figure. This requirement for ex-ante volume estimation often leads to inflated bids, thereby increasing overall procurement costs. Furthermore, the model demonstrates that this design can fail to ensure full system clearance. These findings suggest that the current all-or-none mechanism may be suboptimal for both cost-efficiency and reliability.

This paper establishes a generalization of the Bateman-Horn conjecture within the polynomial analogue, applicable to any field of rational functions over a finite field. The findings indicate that for any finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ and any finite set of polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]$, the count of irreducible polynomials of a specified degree that simultaneously satisfy these sets aligns with the prediction derived from the generalization of the Bateman-Horn conjecture.

Saturn's south pole exhibits a polar stratospheric vortex (PSV) during its summer season, a phenomenon distinct from the winter-focused vortex found at its north pole. This southern summer vortex is characterized by a massive, persistent anticyclonic storm centered on the pole, which generates a complex system of spiraling, counter-rotating bands of wind and temperature. These features generate a dynamic, three-dimensional circulation pattern that facilitates the upward transport of heat and momentum from the mid-latitudes toward the pole. The study utilizes data from the Cassini spacecraft's Composite Infrared Spectrometer (CIRS) to analyze this southern summer vortex, specifically examining the spiraling wind and temperature structures, the associated meridional heat and momentum fluxes, and the resulting poleward shifts in the polar jet. The analysis reveals that the southern summer PSV functions as a significant mechanism for transporting heat and momentum poleward, thereby influencing the thermal and dynamical characteristics of Saturn's polar atmosphere.

This paper introduces a new class of blow-up criteria for the cubic focusing Schrödinger equation in bounded domains, applicable even when the domain boundary disrupts classical techniques. We establish that if the initial data possesses sufficiently high energy relative to the ground state energy within the domain, solutions will blow up in finite time. Our approach relies on a novel local well-posedness result for the cubic focusing problem in exterior regions, which allows us to establish a lower bound on the mass of the concentration of energy.

This paper introduces a theory of positive-characteristic analogues for the classical results in commutative algebra known as the Cayley-Hamilton theorem and the theory of adjoints. These extensions are developed within the framework of characteristic-zero settings, specifically utilizing the theory of adjoints established by M. Auslander and D. Buchsbaum.

We introduce the definition and fundamental properties of symplectical double vector bundles, demonstrating that they function as a symplectical analogue to symmetric $k$-fold vector bundles. We further establish a one-to-one correspondence between symmetric $k$-fold vector bundles and commutative, associative $k$-dialgebras, and prove an analogous result for symplectical $k$-fold vector bundles by defining symplectical dialgebras.

We establish a correspondence between Kirillov's orbit measure and the geometric measure on orbits, utilizing this link to demonstrate that the character formula for the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ is consistent with the formula for the Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{gl}_{N|N}$.

This study introduces a novel phase retrieval algorithm specifically designed for x-ray scattering experiments that employ energy-resolved detectors. The method utilizes the inherent physical constraint that the complex amplitude of the scattered wavefunction must remain constant across the detector surface. By integrating this constraint with a standard iterative approach, the algorithm iteratively reconstructs the energy spectrum. We demonstrate its efficacy through simulations of an ideal detector and through the analysis of data from a real experiment involving a Ni(111) surface. The results indicate that this technique significantly enhances the fidelity of energy spectrum reconstruction, even when dealing with data containing noise.

Blocking fractures, which contain significant reservoirs of oil and gas, are typically modeled using a Dirac-$\delta$ function approach. This study introduces a novel, non-singular function to represent blocking fractures, offering a more realistic depiction of flow dynamics within fractured porous media. This new method is applied to analyze flow in a single blocking fracture, yielding an analytical solution that is subsequently extended to multi-fracture systems. The results demonstrate that this new function provides a superior approximation of the $\delta$-function model compared to existing alternatives. Furthermore, the study investigates the impact of varying fracture positions and blocking characteristics on the productivity of multi-fracture wells.

We introduce a decision-theoretic framework for selecting the most plausible hypothesis from a set of candidates, where each hypothesis $h$ is associated with a utility function $U_h$. This function quantifies the expected utility derived from choosing $h$ given the true state of the world. We examine the optimal strategy for an agent operating under a budget constraint to gather evidence, with the objective of maximizing the expected utility of its final decision. We demonstrate that this problem is equivalent to optimizing the expected value of the highest utility among all hypotheses, using a distribution over evidence-gathering strategies constrained by the budget. We analyze this optimization across two distinct budgeting models: one where the cost of evidence is fixed regardless of the hypothesis, and another where costs vary by hypothesis. In both scenarios, we derive the optimal allocation of the evidence budget. Finally, we validate our theoretical findings through experiments on a text classification task.

We introduce DiscSense, a novel dataset comprising 10,000 instances of annotated semantic relations between sentence pairs, where each pair is drawn from the same news article. This dataset is designed to address the scarcity of resources available for discourse marker detection and discourse relation classification. To evaluate its utility, we conducted experiments on both tasks: first, we developed a baseline model for automatic detection of discourse markers, and second, we assessed the dataset's effectiveness for relation classification. Our findings indicate that DiscSense serves as a valuable resource for advancing research in these areas.

This paper investigates the geometric properties of factorized objective functions within the context of matrix optimization. We establish that if the original objective exhibits restricted strong convexity and smoothness over a specific domain, the factorized version inherits these properties under certain conditions regarding the manifold's curvature and the objective's condition number. Furthermore, we demonstrate that if the original objective is geodesically convex, the factorized form remains geodesically convex provided the curvature is sufficiently bounded and the condition number is adequate. These findings are applicable to a wide array of optimization tasks, including matrix completion, robust PCA, and low-rank regression.

In 1990, Behzad introduced the concept of strong edge-coloring for graphs and conjectured that any bipartite graph with a maximum degree of 3 requires only five colors for a strong edge-coloring. This paper presents the first algorithm capable of constructing a strong edge-coloring for such graphs within $O(n^{2.5})$ time, thereby confirming the conjecture.

This study examines the application of co-evolutionary genetic algorithms (GEAs) to the Prisoner's Dilemma, contrasting individual learning with social learning mechanisms. In the individual learning scenario, the expected Hamming distance separating the population's average strategy from the Nash Equilibrium is found to be larger than that observed in the social learning scenario. Conversely, when analyzing the Hamming distance between the population's average strategy and the Pareto frontier, the individual learning scenario yields a smaller distance compared to the social learning scenario.

This study examines the relationship between the ordinary and symbolic powers of the oriented edge ideal for weighted oriented graphs. Specifically, it establishes that if the ordinary and second symbolic powers of the ideal coincide, then the second symbolic power must equal the ordinary power for all exponents. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that for any bipartite weighted oriented graph, the second symbolic power of the ideal is always identical to its ordinary power.

Neural networks are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, yet silent data corruptions (SDCs)—undetected execution faults that alter internal states—pose a significant threat. This paper introduces a novel approach to SDC prevention by applying non-uniform input range restrictions. We first examine how various activation functions and weight distributions influence the input ranges required to prevent SDCs. Subsequently, we propose a method to restrict inputs such that all activations remain within safe bounds, utilizing a non-uniform restriction strategy that varies across network layers. This approach is designed to minimize the impact on model accuracy while ensuring robustness against corruption. We validate our approach through extensive experiments on ImageNet and CIFAR-10 datasets using ResNet and VGG architectures, demonstrating that the proposed non-uniform restriction achieves a superior balance between robustness and accuracy compared to existing uniform restriction techniques.

We introduce a generalized Jordanian twist applicable to any semisimple Lie algebra, which serves to deform the universal enveloping algebra of the corresponding classical Lie algebra into that of a non-abelian classical r-Lie algebra. We demonstrate that this generalized twist is related to the elementary Jordanian twist via an automorphism of the standard enveloping algebra of the associated classical r-Lie algebra.

Named Entity Recognition (NER) for Named Entity Tagging (NET) in low-resource languages often relies on named entity dictionaries, yet existing methods suffer from poor performance when handling unseen words. This study introduces a novel approach that leverages named entity dictionaries alongside character-level bidirectional long short-term memory (CRNN) networks to enhance NET performance for low-resource languages. By integrating CRNNs, the method effectively captures both local and global contextual information, enabling more accurate identification of unseen words. Evaluated on Vietnamese and Indonesian datasets, the proposed approach demonstrates superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art techniques.

This study examines the evolution of particle ratios across collision systems ranging from small to large scales, specifically analyzing the transition from proton-antiproton ($p$-$\bar{p}$) dominance to pion ($\pi$) prevalence. We investigate the underlying mechanisms driving these changes, with a particular focus on the impact of pion absorption and the associated energy loss. Our analysis reveals that pion absorption is a critical factor in accounting for the observed increase in pion yields as system size increases. Additionally, we explore the influence of varying initial conditions, such as the multiplicity of produced particles, on these ratios. The findings suggest that the multiplicity of pions plays a significant role in shaping particle ratio distributions. Finally, we discuss the implications of these results for understanding the properties of the quark-gluon plasma and the subsequent hadronization process.

We introduce a novel framework for analyzing the relationship between a city's infrastructure topology and the dynamics of civil unrest. Our approach models the city as a complex network where nodes represent districts and edges signify the connectivity between them. We hypothesize that the topological arrangement of this network influences the propagation of dissent, which we model as a contagion process. By integrating a standard Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible (SIS) model with a spatially explicit, topology-aware simulation, we examine how network structure affects the spread of unrest. Our findings indicate that the city's infrastructure topology significantly impacts both the prevalence and the spatial distribution of dissent. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the specific arrangement of connections can either facilitate or impede the containment of civil unrest.

This paper introduces a symbolic decision procedure for determining whether one regular expression is contained within another. The approach combines Brzozowski's operator with Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solving to handle the symbolic representation of infinite state spaces. By treating the operator as a SAT theory, the method translates the containment problem into a satisfiability instance. The resulting decision procedure is also adaptable for computing the most general regular subexpression of a given expression $E$ with respect to a set of expressions $F$.

This paper introduces a novel visual-inertial odometry (VIO) algorithm that leverages deep learning to enhance robustness and accuracy. Unlike conventional VIO methods that rely on hand-crafted features, this approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract robust visual features. Furthermore, it employs a recurrent neural network (RNN) to integrate inertial data, thereby improving the fusion of visual and inertial information. The algorithm was evaluated on the EuRoC dataset and compared against state-of-the-art VIO algorithms. Results indicate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy and robustness, particularly in challenging environments characterized by high dynamic motion and varying lighting conditions.

"Square-root topology," a concept introduced by the author, describes three-dimensional systems hosting higher-order Weyl semimetals, which are characterized by the coexistence of second-order bulk topological invariants and first-order surface Fermi arcs. This work establishes a direct connection between these second-order invariants and the first-order ones, revealing that the latter are determined by the former. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the second-order bulk invariants serve as the origin of the first-order surface Fermi arcs, which terminate at the endpoints of second-order bulk topological lines. Finally, the paper proposes a new classification scheme for higher-order topological semimetals based on the interplay between these distinct topological lines and line nodes.

This study examines a data completion problem where the objective is to infer missing values for a function defined on a subset of a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, given known values on the subdomain and partial information on the complement. The approach employs a variational framework utilizing edge finite elements to construct a discrete system. A key advantage of this method is its ability to naturally accommodate various types of missing data through the strategic selection of edge finite element degrees of freedom. Furthermore, the proposed scheme ensures a symmetric positive definite linear system, which can be efficiently solved using standard iterative solvers. Numerical experiments demonstrate the method's efficacy in resolving diverse missing data scenarios.

Knowledge amalgamation, which involves training a student model to master the knowledge contained within one or more teacher models, has garnered significant attention. However, the inherent computational demands of this process often hinder its widespread adoption. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a streamlined training framework grounded in saliency analysis. This approach prioritizes the most influential training samples, allowing the student model to concentrate its learning efforts on these high-impact data points. Furthermore, we integrate a dynamic sample weighting mechanism that adjusts the importance of selected samples throughout the training lifecycle. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that this method not only achieves a student model with performance nearly on par with full-scale knowledge distillation but also delivers these results with substantially reduced computational resources.

This paper presents the explicit construction of exactly 1,000,000 $\mathbb{Q}$-quartic field extensions where the ranks of two specific elliptic curves do not increase. These fields are characterized by having a rational rank of 2 and containing no quadratic subfields. The result serves as a specialized case of a broader theorem applicable to any collection of elliptic curves defined over number fields.

We examine the generation of irreversible entropy during quantum quenches within a free scalar field theory, specifically in a spatially infinite one-dimensional system initially prepared in its ground state. By utilizing the Wigner function formalism, we derive an expression for irreversible entropy that depends on the change in total entropy and the initial temperature. Furthermore, we establish a connection between this irreversible entropy and the quantity known as "warming." Our analysis reveals that, for quenches characterized by a large coupling constant, the irreversible entropy increases linearly with the system's size, indicating a positive scaling with the thermodynamic limit.

We establish a connection between the distinguishability time for non-unitary dynamics and the time required to purify the system-environment state through time-twirling. Specifically, we demonstrate that the distinguishability time is bounded by a function of the purification time associated with the time-twirled initial state-environment composite. This result is applied to analyze the dynamics of a quantum walk on an open directed graph, where we derive a bound for the distinguishability time based on the parameters of the walk.

This paper investigates the existence of regular simplices within the unit cube $Q_n$ under interpolation constraints. Specifically, it examines whether a regular, nondegenerate simplex can be formed by $d+1$ points in $Q_n$ such that each point shares at least one coordinate with a specified set of $d$ nodes, where $d \leq n$. The study establishes that if the number of nodes $d$ satisfies $d \leq n - \sqrt{2}$, then such a regular simplex necessarily exists. Conversely, it is demonstrated that when $d = n - \lfloor\sqrt{2}\rfloor$, no regular simplex can exist that satisfies the interpolation conditions for every possible configuration of the nodes.

This study examines the electrical characteristics of silicon wafers treated with a buffer oxide layer, which is removed using a wet etching process. The primary objective is to evaluate the impact of this specific etching method on the surface morphology and bulk electrical properties of the silicon. The investigation focuses on two primary parameters: surface roughness and carrier concentration. Surface roughness was quantified using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), while carrier concentration was determined via Hall Effect measurements. The results indicate that the buffer oxide wet etching process effectively eliminates surface defects and contaminants, yielding a surface with low roughness. Furthermore, the study confirms that this technique preserves the silicon's bulk electrical properties, resulting in a carrier concentration that is comparable to that of standard buffer oxide etched silicon.

We present a coupled interior-exterior model designed to simulate the atmospheric evolution of terrestrial planets, specifically focusing on the interaction between a planet's atmosphere and its interior. The atmospheric component utilizes a one-dimensional radiative-convective model, while the interior component employs a two-layer system consisting of a solid lithosphere and a fluid interior. This framework allows for the investigation of how interior-exterior cycling influences long-term atmospheric evolution. We examine the model's behavior under varying conditions, including changes in stellar luminosity, the presence of a magnetic field, and different initial atmospheric states. Furthermore, we explore the impact of interior composition, specifically the presence of a metallic core versus a silicate core, on the system's dynamics.

This paper introduces a nonlinear multivariate Hawkes process designed to model complex interactions within multivariate point processes. The model incorporates a nonlinear self-excitation component alongside linear cross-excitation effects from other variables. We establish the existence and uniqueness of solutions for this process and derive its stationary distribution under specific conditions. Furthermore, we develop an efficient simulation algorithm and prove the consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator. Finally, we apply the model to analyze call data from the stock market, demonstrating its ability to capture nonlinear self-excitation and inter-variable interactions.

We introduce a plasma waveplate capable of rotating linearly polarized light into circular polarization, functioning as a key element for diagnosing tokamak edge-localized modes (ELMs). This device relies on a plasma layer situated within a magnetic field, where the thickness $d$ must satisfy $d \geq \lambda/4$ to achieve a $\pi/2$ phase shift. Crucially, this thickness is inversely proportional to both the plasma electron density and the magnetic field strength. We demonstrate that a plasma layer with an electron density of $10^{17} \text{ m}^{-3}$, confined by a 2 Tesla magnetic field, can rotate linear polarization by 90 degrees within a 10 cm region. This configuration is feasible in the scrape-off layer of a tokamak, such as DIII-D, during the inter-ELM interval.

We investigate the type-II two-Higgs doublet extension of the Standard Model, incorporating complex parameters in the scalar potential to generate CP violation. We examine the potential magnitude of the tau electric dipole moment (EDM) and the CP asymmetry in $B_c$ meson decays. Our findings indicate that, within this framework, the tau EDM can reach approximately $10^{-17}$ e$\cdot$cm, while the CP asymmetry in $B_c$ meson decays may attain values near 1%.

This paper investigates the error correction properties of rank metric codes, specifically analyzing the distinct behaviors observed at rates $R < 1/2$ versus $R > 1/2$. For rates below the threshold, the study derives a general formula for the expected number of symbol errors correctable by a code with rate $R$, demonstrating that this value increases as the rate rises. Conversely, for rates exceeding $1/2$, the analysis reveals that the expected number of correctable symbol errors remains constant regardless of the specific code rate. These findings are supported by extensive numerical simulations.

We examine the relationship between geodesic operators defined on the AdS$_{2}$ and AdS$_{3}$ bulk spaces and conserved current OPE blocks within a two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT$_{2}$). We demonstrate that while AdS$_{2}$ geodesic operators are constructed from a single Virasoro primary geodesic operator, AdS$_{3}$ geodesic operators are instead formed by a linear combination of two distinct primary geodesic operators.

This manifold carries a specific differential structure defined by Gelfand-Zakharov and later by Fock, which is crucial for analyzing the cohomology of combinatorial configuration spaces. In this work, we introduce a novel combinatorial differential manifold, termed the Gelfand-MacPherson-Hodge manifold, designed to model the cohomology of configuration spaces of points in a vector space equipped with a specific cohomology class.

Lobster-eye optics (LEO) are promising candidates for next-generation X-ray telescopes, yet their precise alignment and characterization remain difficult. This study introduces a novel method for diagnosing LEO systems using a simple, low-cost setup consisting of a point source, a single LEO module, and a single flat-panel X-ray detector. The technique leverages the distinctive "cross-like" image formed by the LEO, analyzing its ellipticity and azimuthal rotation angle to determine the precise location of the source relative to the LEO. Specifically, the azimuthal rotation angle allows for the identification of specific segments of the LEO. We validated this approach through both computer simulations and physical experiments, demonstrating that the method can accurately pinpoint the source position with a spatial resolution of approximately 10 cm.

This paper introduces a novel level set methodology for examining second-order fully nonlinear equations, specifically those that are elliptic or parabolic. We apply this framework to investigate the well-posedness of Dirichlet problems on bounded domains for both elliptic and parabolic variants of the fully nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman-Isaacs (HJBI) equation. Additionally, we examine the well-posedness of parabolic HJBI equation initial value problems. Our approach relies on establishing a priori estimates for the solution and its gradient, alongside a priori estimates for the viscosity solution of the associated frozen coefficient linearized equations. These estimates are derived by analyzing the level set formulation of the problem, which involves a system of fully nonlinear first-order equations. This system is constructed by linearizing the original second-order fully nonlinear equation along a specific solution trajectory.

This study examines halo mass predictions for cosmological simulations featuring an initial amplitude of scalar perturbations ($A_s$) of $0.002$, a value significantly higher than that used in standard simulations. We analyze the impact of varying $A_s$ on halo mass estimation using both a density-only model and a combined model incorporating density and tidal fields. Our findings indicate that a density-only model yields a halo mass function with a root-mean-square scatter of approximately $0.07$ dex for $A_s = 0.002$, a figure that rises to roughly $0.08$ dex when $A_s$ is $0.0002$. Furthermore, we observe that increasing $A_s$ leads to a systematic underestimation of halo mass by the density-only model, an effect that becomes more pronounced at higher mass scales. Conversely, the inclusion of tidal fields in the model effectively mitigates both the increased scatter and the mass underestimation caused by elevated $A_s$.

We introduce a novel Eulerian approach for modeling rotating stars, wherein specific angular momentum and mass are assigned to fixed Eulerian grid cells. This method employs a new formulation of the hydrostatic equilibrium equations, which are solved iteratively to determine the initial model. Subsequent time evolution is achieved using a standard Lagrangian hydrodynamics code, with mass and specific angular momentum conserved within each Eulerian cell via a flux-based scheme. This technique offers a more straightforward and physically consistent method for handling mass and specific angular momentum compared to traditional strategies. We demonstrate its application to a differentially rotating, convective stellar model, successfully establishing a hydrostatic initial configuration and accurately simulating the angular momentum transport driven by the shear instability.

Selective labeling is a cost-effective strategy for acquiring labeled data by prioritizing the annotation of the most informative samples. This approach is especially advantageous when labeling expenses are high, as it concentrates resources on key instances. However, existing methods often require the model to access the entire pool of unlabeled data, which can be problematic for large-scale datasets stored in distributed environments. To address this limitation, we introduce Selective Labeling with Federated Learning (SLFL), a framework designed to identify and label the most valuable samples while preserving data privacy. SLFL integrates selective labeling principles with federated learning, enabling the selection of high-value samples exclusively from local devices without revealing raw data to a central server. We evaluate SLFL across three distinct datasets and multiple machine learning algorithms, demonstrating its efficacy in both centralized and federated settings. Furthermore, we assess the method's robustness regarding selective labeling parameters and the impact of selective labeling on model convergence.

This study examines the electromagnetic signatures arising from the coalescence of two neutron stars, specifically focusing on the afterglow produced by the relativistic jet and the afterglow generated by the interaction between the ejecta and the surrounding medium. We analyze the spectral characteristics of the afterglow, the temporal evolution of the afterglow, and the observable signatures of the kilonova. The pandemic's legacy extends beyond immediate health and economic impacts, fundamentally reshaping the variety of urban interactions and the adaptability of communities. This study examines how the crisis altered the diversity of encounters in public spaces, a critical element for urban life. Drawing on a survey of 1,000 French residents, the authors analyze shifts in the frequency and nature of public activities, alongside changes in individual mobility patterns. The findings indicate that pandemic-induced modifications to daily routines and movement habits have persisted well into the post-pandemic era. These enduring effects have led to a measurable decline in the diversity of urban encounters and a corresponding reduction in the resilience of urban communities.

We investigate the inner regions of circumstellar discs surrounding high-mass young stellar objects, specifically examining how migrating objects influence the inner disc's stability and dynamics. Our findings indicate that even a single embedded object with a mass of 0.01 Earth masses ($0.01\,M_{\oplus}$) can trigger rapid, chaotic scattering of inner disc particles. This scattering occurs on timescales significantly shorter than the viscous evolution timescale of the inner disc, leading to a near-complete evacuation of the inner region. We further demonstrate that the presence of such an object can facilitate the inward transport of dust and pebbles, potentially enabling the formation of terrestrial planets within the innermost parts of these discs.

This study introduces a novel method for determining the free surface elevation in water wave scenarios, utilizing only the wave envelope derived from the velocity potential. This potential is obtained via the linearized boundary condition, while the envelope itself is reconstructed from surface elevation measurements using a Hilbert transform. The proposed approach involves an iterative algorithm that applies the inverse of the envelope-to-elevation operator to the measured envelope, thereby recovering the elevation. The validity of this algorithm is confirmed through numerical simulations of both linear and fully nonlinear wave problems.

This paper introduces a surface layer theorem applicable to differential forms defined on locally convex spaces. This result serves as a foundational element for establishing the generalized Stokes theorem within the same context.

This paper introduces a layered control system designed for mobile platforms that utilize sonar data to navigate autonomously toward a target. The architecture integrates a high-level layer responsible for generating reference trajectories based on sonar inputs with a low-level layer that manages the execution of these trajectories. Simulation results demonstrate the system's ability to navigate a platform through an obstacle-filled environment while maintaining a constant distance from detected obstacles.

This study introduces a novel approach to fake news detection that integrates contextual information alongside textual content. We propose a new metric, Contextual Relatedness (CR), to quantify the relevance between a news item and its associated context. Our method involves retrieving the top-$k$ most related items from a news graph and feeding them, along with the target news, into a BERT-based classifier. Experiments conducted on the Fake or Real News (FOR) dataset demonstrate that this framework significantly outperforms existing baselines.

We examine the interplay between curvature effects and hysteresis within a system of interacting particles confined to a spherical surface. We demonstrate that increasing curvature induces a rise in system entropy, which in turn promotes the formation of a disordered, glassy state. This transition to disorder manifests as an increase in the width of the hysteresis loop. We further analyze the geometric origins of this curvature-driven behavior, showing that it results from a shift in the system's preferred configurations.

This paper introduces a novel two-block alternating minimization approach to address the $L_1$-PCA problem after its reformulation. The proposed method is proven to converge to a stationary point, and numerical experiments demonstrate that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Paraphrase tasks, which involve generating semantically equivalent sentences from a source, serve as a powerful tool for assessing the reliability of annotated data in semantic labeling. This paper introduces a method that leverages paraphrase generation to identify and correct inconsistencies within existing label sets. We propose a framework for semantic labeling that integrates paraphrase generation to detect and rectify erroneous annotations. We evaluate this approach on the MSRA dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving label consistency.

Global metric maps (GMMs) are widely recognized for their effectiveness in navigation, yet their global nature often leads to suboptimal global planning and high computational costs for updating. Conversely, HiTMap offers a hierarchical, tile-based global representation that facilitates efficient local navigation and rapid updates. This paper introduces HiTMap-GMM, a novel framework that merges HiTMap's advantages with the robustness of global metric maps. By integrating global metric maps within individual HiTMap tiles, the proposed method enables precise local navigation and effective map updates. Furthermore, HiTMap-GMM employs a hierarchical global planning strategy that leverages the tiles' inherent structure to generate optimal global trajectories. Experimental results demonstrate that HiTMap-GMM outperforms existing global planning algorithms in both computational efficiency and path quality.

Atomic interferometry has recently enabled the detection of extremely weak local magnetic fields, with sensitivities reaching approximately 100 nG/√Hz. This study demonstrates that the technique can achieve even greater sensitivity by integrating a local field sensor into the interferometer. By utilizing a Mach-Zehnder configuration with a spatially separated sensor, the system detects fields at the nanogauss level across a 100 μm diameter area with a bandwidth of 1 Hz. Furthermore, the method is capable of mapping fields with a spatial resolution of 10 μm and a sensitivity of 100 nG/√Hz.

We examine the application of Bayesian methods to population admixture analysis, specifically focusing on the use of a Dirichlet process prior placed on population densities. Our investigation reveals that this prior induces a clustering effect on the admixture proportions, grouping distinct source populations into identical clusters. Consequently, the resulting posterior distribution yields identifiable admixture weights only for these clusters rather than for individual source populations. We demonstrate that this clustering phenomenon arises from the prior's tendency to concentrate mass on a finite set of points. Finally, we introduce a modified Bayesian framework utilizing a Dirichlet process prior on the population density that mitigates this concentration, thereby preserving the identifiability of admixture weights for each distinct population.

GPU memory allocators typically rely on first-fit strategies, which often result in suboptimal memory utilization and fragmentation. To address this, we introduce **DynaSOAr**, a GPU memory allocator that employs a dynamic, size-oriented first-fit approach. DynaSOAr dynamically adjusts the number of free-lists based on the distribution of allocation requests, ensuring that each list manages blocks of similar sizes. This design enables the allocator to quickly identify the most suitable free block for any given request. Furthermore, DynaSOAr incorporates a novel, high-performance block coalescing technique that consolidates fragmented memory regions in real time, maintaining a compact and efficient free memory layout. Evaluation against standard GPU allocators demonstrates that DynaSOAr achieves a 10% reduction in memory fragmentation and delivers a 1.5x speedup in allocation and deallocation operations.

We present a theoretical investigation into the interplay between spin-orbit coupling and magnetic impurities within the context of topological superconductivity. Specifically, we examine how spin-orbit coupling influences the spatial distribution and energy levels of Yu-Sharapa-Ryazov (YSR) states induced by magnetic adatoms or dimers on a topological superconductor surface. Our findings indicate that spin-orbit coupling shifts the positions of YSR state peaks in both real and momentum space. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this effect can be leveraged to determine the precise location of magnetic adatoms or dimers with high accuracy.

We report the discovery of three transiting mini-Neptunes orbiting the K-dwarf star TOI-700 (TOI-700.1), with orbital periods ranging from 10 to 20 days. These planets, designated TOI-700 b, c, and d, possess radii between 1.8 and 2.3 Earth radii and masses between 5.5 and 11.5 Earth masses, implying bulk densities from 1.8 to 3.5 g/cm³. The system's architecture is notable for its compactness, with all planets residing within the star's habitable zone. We present a dynamical stability analysis of this configuration, demonstrating that the system remains stable only if the outermost planet, TOI-700 d, maintains a specific orbital eccentricity. Furthermore, we evaluate the system's potential for detecting atmospheric signals via transmission spectroscopy, concluding that the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) could identify atmospheric constituents in the atmospheres of planets c and d.

We investigated the structural and electronic characteristics of carbon and nitrogen within TiO$_2$ using first-principles calculations. Our analysis reveals that both carbon and nitrogen exhibit higher formation energies in interstitial sites compared to substitutional sites. Furthermore, interstitial configurations display a reduced band gap alongside increased magnetic moments relative to their substitutional analogs. Specifically, the band gap narrows from 2.8 eV to 1.6 eV for carbon and from 2.8 eV to 1.4 eV for nitrogen. Additionally, the magnetic moments increase from 0.0 $\mu_B$ to 1.0 $\mu_B$ for carbon and from 0.0 $\mu_B$ to 1.4 $\mu_B$ for nitrogen. Finally, we determined the most stable interstitial positions for both dopants to be located at the octahedral voids.

This study examines the flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) decays of the top quark, specifically $t \to Hc$ and $t \to Zc$, utilizing data collected at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV from proton-proton collisions at the LHC. The analysis focuses on events where a single top quark is produced in association with a charm quark and either a Higgs boson or a Z boson, with the Higgs decaying into bottom quarks and the Z decaying into leptons. The analysis covers integrated luminosities of 139 fb$^{-1}$ and 92 fb$^{-1}$ for $tH(c)$ and $tZ(c)$ processes, respectively. The results indicate branching ratio limits for the $t \to Hc$ decay of less than $1.6 \times 10^{-2}$ and for the $t \to Zc$ decay of less than $1.1 \times 10^{-2}$, both at a 95% confidence level.

This paper investigates the problem of determining the minimum number of colors required to color the edges of a graph $G$ such that no monochromatic copy of a graph $F$ exists. We establish a general lower bound for this number, denoted as $\chi^c(G, F)$, which is at least $|E(G)| / \left( \Delta(G)^{|V(F)| - 1} \cdot \max_{v \in V(F)} d_F(v)^{|V(F)| - 1} \right)$, where $\Delta(G)$ represents the maximum degree of $G$ and $d_F(v)$ is the degree of vertex $v$ within $F$. This bound is tight when $G$ is a complete graph. Furthermore, we derive an improved lower bound specifically for triangles, showing that $\chi^c(K_n, K_3)$ is at least $n/2$.

We compare the noise resilience of qubits and qutrits for determining the mass of a harmonic oscillator. We find that, under amplitude damping and phase damping noise, qutrits exhibit superior tolerance to noise-induced mass determination errors. However, under amplitude damping, a qubit coupled to an ancillary qutrit demonstrates the highest robustness.

We report the observation of a high level of positron polarization, reaching a degree exceeding 30%, generated via the annihilation of polarized electrons with an unpolarized positronium beam. This level of polarization surpasses that of the incident electron beam. The findings demonstrate that this technique is capable of producing a highly polarized positron beam, a capability that could facilitate significant future research, such as the study of the magnetic dipole moment of the positron.

We establish that groups featuring a polynomial diameter of at least degree 3 must contain infinitely many conjugacy classes, as well as infinitely many non-isomorphic nilpotent subgroups. Furthermore, we demonstrate that groups with a polynomial diameter possess a finite asymptotic conjugacy width.

This study introduces a compact, low-cost temperature sensor utilizing a 0.18-$\mu$m CMOS process, featuring a 200-$\mu$m$\times$200-$\mu$m die area. The design employs a 200-element differential current-to-voltage converter array, where the array's inaccuracy is mitigated through a 12-bit successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The sensor achieves a 12-bit resolution with a 1.5 V supply, sampling at 1.5 kS/s while consuming 1.2 mW of power. Post-layout simulations conducted in 0.18-$\mu$m CMOS technology demonstrate that the sensor operates with a 1.5 V supply, 1.2 mW power consumption, and a 1.5 kS/s sampling rate. The system occupies a 0.004 mm$^2$ die area and delivers 1.5 kS/s sampling at 1.5 V supply, 1.2 mW power consumption, and a 0.004 mm$^2$ die area.
